audits.title: 75. Less is More: A Physician-Driven Quality Improvement Stewardship Initiative to Reduce Excessive Duration of Antibiotic Therapy in Veterans Hospitalized with Community-Acquired Pneumonia
audits.standard: IDSA/ATS CAP guidelines: 5 days of therapy for clinically stable patients; aim to reduce median duration by at least 1 day in 5 months
audits.setting: Inner-city Veterans Affairs hospital (John D Dingell VA Medical Center), Detroit
audits.intervention: Chief Resident in Quality and Safety gave monthly education and daily audit and feedback with patient-specific duration recommendations.
audits.other_findings: Total antibiotic duration and excess days fell without adverse effect on outcomes.
audits.citation: Monday L, Yazdanpanah O, Sokolowski C, Sebastian J, Kuhn R, Kareem B, et al.. 75. Less is More: A Physician-Driven Quality Improvement Stewardship Initiative to Reduce Excessive Duration of Antibiotic Therapy in Veterans Hospitalized with Community-Acquired Pneumonia. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2020;7(Suppl 1):S55-S56.

audits.title: O01 Auditing the duration of antibiotic therapy for children treated as inpatients for community acquired pneumonia
audits.standard: Trust guidelines: 5–7 days of amoxicillin for simple community-acquired pneumonia
audits.setting: Paediatric inpatient ward, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Median antibiotic duration 7 days (range 1–9); 7 children (23.3%) received more than 7 days. 40% amoxicillin only, 26.7% co-amoxiclav only, 33.3% combinations.

audits.intervention: Trust guideline changed via Paediatric Microguide to allow a 3-day amoxicillin course.
audits.other_findings: 9 of 28 children with chest x-ray (32.1%) had no focal changes but all received antibiotics. Re-audit planned for winter 2022–23.
audits.citation: . O01 Auditing the duration of antibiotic therapy for children treated as inpatients for community acquired pneumonia. JAC Antimicrob Resist. 2023;5(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Audit of antibiotic prescribing practices for pediatric pneumonia in the outpatient department: focus on amoxicillin and azithromycin.
audits.standard: WHO AWaRe and IMNCI guidance on antibiotic choice, dose and duration
audits.setting: Outpatient department, Children Hospital Sukkur (Sindh Institute of Child Health and Neonatology)

cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed 116/132 (87.9%); amoxicillin 26/132 (19.7%), appropriate 1/26 (3.8%); azithromycin 66/132 (50.0%), appropriate 20/66 (30.3%).

audits.other_findings: Objective diagnostic criteria were inconsistently recorded and follow-up rates stayed low (about 15%).

audits.title: Shortening treatment duration for uncomplicated community acquired pneumonia to align with best practice guidelines in a large academic paediatric emergency department.
audits.standard: Updated recommendation for 5-day antibiotic therapy for community-acquired pneumonia
audits.setting: Paediatric emergency department, UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh
audits.intervention: Educational outreach, data sharing, on-site reminders and audit-and-feedback.
audits.other_findings: ED return visits were monitored for treatment failure.

audits.title: Impact of a Personalized Audit and Feedback Intervention on Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Outpatient Pediatric Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
audits.standard: Guideline-concordant antibiotics for paediatric community-acquired pneumonia

cycle1.result: Non-guideline-concordant antibiotics in 22/103 (21.4%) of control patients aged 5 years or over.

audits.intervention: Monthly personalised audit and feedback to primary care providers for 6 months.

cycle2.result: Non-guideline-concordant antibiotics in 3/51 (5.9%) of intervention patients aged 5 years or over (P < .05).

audits.other_findings: Comparison was a concurrent control group rather than a before-and-after re-audit.
audits.citation: Diaz MCG, Handy LK, Crutchfield JH Jr, Cadilla A, Hossain J, Werk LN. Impact of a Personalized Audit and Feedback Intervention on Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Outpatient Pediatric Community-Acquired Pneumonia. Clin Pediatr (Phila). 2020;59(11):988-994. doi:10.1177/0009922820928054. PMID: 32486840.

audits.title: Comparison of procalcitonin testing to a targeted audit-and-feedback strategy on prescribed durations of therapy for community-acquired pneumonia.
audits.standard: 5 days of therapy for uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia
audits.setting: Two community teaching hospitals, Mercy Health Saint Mary's

cycle1.result: Average duration of therapy 7.0 days (TAF site) and 7.8 days (PCT site).

audits.intervention: Targeted audit and feedback recommending 5 days at one site; procalcitonin testing with routine audit and feedback at the other.

cycle2.result: Average duration of therapy 5.5 days (TAF) and 5.4 days (PCT), p = 0.8.

audits.other_findings: No differences in patient outcomes between strategies.
audits.citation: Clark LT, Beuschel TS, Buss PM, Jameson AP, Dumkow LE. Comparison of procalcitonin testing to a targeted audit-and-feedback strategy on prescribed durations of therapy for community-acquired pneumonia. Diagn Microbiol Infect Dis. 2021;99(1):115202. doi:10.1016/j.diagmicrobio.2020.115202. PMID: 33007583.

audits.title: A Physician-Driven Quality Improvement Stewardship Intervention Using Lean Six Sigma Improves Patient Care for Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
audits.standard: IDSA recommendation of a minimum of 5 days of antibiotic therapy in stable patients with community-acquired pneumonia
audits.setting: Single-centre inpatient setting, John D Dingell Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Detroit

cycle1.result: Median antibiotic days of therapy per patient 8 days.

audits.intervention: Lean Six Sigma (DMAIC) physician-driven stewardship intervention: education, prospective audit and feedback from a physician peer, and daily tracking of excess days of therapy on a Kaizen board.

cycle2.result: Median antibiotic days of therapy per patient 5 days (8 versus 5 days; p value truncated in abstract).

audits.other_findings: No differences in clinical outcomes including Clostridioides difficile infection were observed; almost half of caregivers surveyed knew that 5 days of treatment could be appropriate.
audits.citation: Monday LM, Yazdanpaneh O, Sokolowski C, Chi J, Kuhn R, Bazzy K, et al.. A Physician-Driven Quality Improvement Stewardship Intervention Using Lean Six Sigma Improves Patient Care for Community-Acquired Pneumonia. Glob J Qual Saf Healthc. 2021;4(3):109-116. doi:10.36401/jqsh-21-2. PMID: 37261063.
